risk_if_not_implemented: Without Software Design Root Cause Analysis (RCA), applications may be built and deployed with exploitable design and coding weaknesses that adversaries can leverage. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Incident Persistence / Recurrence (R-IR-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Conformity Monitoring
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to validate that Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) conform to the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements.
compensating_control_1.justification: Conformity Monitoring (CPL-05) provides periodic assessment and assurance that compensates for the absence of Software Design Root Cause Analysis (TDA-05.5) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Secure Engineering Principles
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of industry-recognized security, compliance and resilience practices in the specification, design, development, implementation and modification of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
compensating_control_2.justification: Secure Engineering Principles (SEA-05) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Software Design Root Cause Analysis (TDA-05.5) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
